body:
FOUND BY MYK, 2026-07-26, first thing in the morning: he opened a served store's root in a browser and got `{"errors":["a bearer token is required, and this one opens nothing"]}`. Two defects in one small surface, and the poetry rule (errors are first-class craft) owns both:

(1) THE MESSAGE OVERPROMISES. No bearer token opens `/` — there is no route there; the mounts are the doors. A refusal that names a remedy which would not work is a false report in miniature.

(2) THE MOST HUMAN-VISITED PATH IS THE LEAST HUMAN ANSWER. The first thing anyone does with a served store's URL is open its root in a browser. The uniform-refusal discipline (a mount that exists and one that does not must answer identically to a tokenless caller — dynamic-mounts rails pin this) applies to MOUNT paths and does not require the bare root to be rude: a greeting that names NO mount enumerates nothing.

THE SHAPE: `GET /` (and probably `GET /favicon.ico` → 204, since every browser asks) answers a small static page or text: a Loam store serves here; its doors are at `/:mount`; what an operator has declared public answers without a token; everything else wants one. Content-negotiate if cheap (text/html for browsers, JSON for curl), or just serve HTML — a human is the only caller with a reason to GET `/`.

CARE: the greeting must be CONSTANT — independent of how many mounts exist, what they are named, and whether any public declaration exists — or it becomes an oracle. The rail is two-sided: the greeting is identical for a store with three mounts and a store with none (delta level: byte-identical body), AND every existing uniform-refusal rail in `test/server/dynamic-mounts.test.ts` stays untouched and green (those are frozen — do not edit them; new rails in a new file).

Self-merge bar: this changes what `/` answers, which no spec section promises today — it is a new tiny surface, so flag it in the PR and let Myk glance at the words themselves; the words are the deliverable.
title: The front door greets a browser like a curl — give `/` a true, warm, non-enumerating answer
